relevance_note: Single-patient case report of fish-eye disease with two LCAT variants: "the patient is compound heterozygous for variants in different LCAT alleles, confirming the diagnosis of FED".
method_note: Read the whole paper (no tables; text and a short supplementary alt-text). Built the JSON with a small script from my own reading. In scope: the patient and her paternal grandmother, who is described as affected ('reportedly had a history of corneal opacification') but untested; she has no variant rows. 'No other family members exhibited similar ocular findings' names no individuals, so it creates no rows. Normal findings recorded as excluded abnormalities per D-27 (triglycerides, VLDL-C, apoB, CE/TC ratio, IOP, visual acuity). Screening for 'renal dysfunction' was unremarkable: used to exclude 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure' only; proteinuria, hematuria and nephrotic syndrome left not reported. 'Hepatic dysfunction' and 'dilated fundus examination unremarkable' recorded as written. Total cholesterol was within normal range (155 mg/dL) while the history lists hypercholesterolemia controlled with atorvastatin; no 'elevated total cholesterol' excluded row was emitted to avoid implying a contradiction (treatment status at measurement not stated). Zygosity recorded as 'compound heterozygous' from the authors' own statement; each variant is also called heterozygous. Supplement alt-text says the findings 'indicate a potentially positive carrier status', which is in tension with the main text's compound heterozygous diagnosis (phase not stated as tested). Inheritance not reported: no family testing. Corneal thickness reported differently by Scheimpflug (419/409 µm) and OCT (479/470 µm); both quoted. Abstract says CE ratio 'remained within the normal range'; Discussion says 'at the lower end of the range'.
